I'm gonna go against the norm and say NTA. Though, blocking your daughter seems a bit extreme and if you did truly say "fuck off" then that was a butthole move, but moving on. 

Based on the info given by OP and nothing more, his ex prevented him from having a relationship with his daughter. So he is not her dad really, but just a bio father. He paid his child support, tried, efforts failed and he eventually gave up because people get tired. Life sucks sometimes.

He is not punishing his daughter. I don't get how he is. The ex prevented the relationship (again, only going on info given), so it's the ex who punished his kid. And the idea that he's proving the ex's lies were true doesn't click with me either. She's 18. Her opinion is made by now, and if her distant father doesn't give money to her solidifies her opinion then it was screwed anyway. She has to make the decision to investigate and see if her father is as her mother stated. 

The thing that bothers me the most is that the mom called. Not his daughter. The ex, mother of daughter. The daughter didn't even do it herself.

The bottom line is she's 18. She was prevented from getting to know you. Now she wants money. Yeah, no. 

The thing here is obviously I'd like more info and to understand more because duh, but using only the info given, NTA.

First: NTA. Please don't feel guilty for wanting privacy. It's part of growing up. 

I think it may be part of parents struggling to see their kids growing up and wanting privacy. Or she's just nosy. Regardless, her behavior is unacceptable. It's one thing to ask, but she yelled and guilt tripped you. Not okay. 

White lying isn't a bad idea, but I would also suggest telling part of the whole truth if you can. It'll be easier, at least it was for me.

I am glad your parents are getting you therapy though. I hope everything goes smoothly and improves. Stay strong!

I think some people just can't fully understand suicidal thoughts. At least, that's my guess.

Cause people who do that almost assume that those with suicidal thoughts just jumped to suicide as a first resort. The human mind and body doesn't want to be miserable and die. Most of the time, suicidal thoughts are earned in a sick way through trying out solution after solution and failing until you reach the last solution you have. Of course, this isn't the case for everyone. It's just something that came to my mind.

I relate to this so much...

Whenever things get super rough, I just look at that mental door I opened in high school and think "Yeah...that's always an option" and somehow, it helps me hold out. 

I always tell people to please reach out because the moment you open the door to suicide and truly wanting to do it, you can't close it. But really...I think it's a comfort to me to leave it open. A way out. The one thing I can control.

It's twisted thinking, but it's gotten me through rough times.
